# Bounded coherent-reference content observation contract

**AI disclosure:** Generated by AI, retaining the original z23 proposal and correcting it
through maintainer review. **Design only. No capture tool, device access or authorization
is supplied here.** `observation.py` validates synthetic contract fixtures, not real host
state. A caller saying “coherent” is not proof; a future adapter must derive each fact from
verified allocation records, source identity and live queue/lifetime state.

## Question and admitted path

At CRA decode28/POC32 and the first-bad consumers (Gst decode29/POC28, VA decode31/POC31),
which bytes in compressed/MV ranges are stable within a run, across off/on observations,
and across repeated runs/clients? PR76 establishes equality of copied controls with the
same-run successful ioctl returns and selected command words with pinned C. It does not
establish equality of every command or every byte the firmware reads.

The original “copy after DQBUF; userspace owns the plane” proposal is insufficient. DQBUF
completes the writer but does not exclude later reference readers. The first implementation
must be **coherent/noncached only**, with no in-flight work on the selected allocation.
The exact pinned vb2 exporter has no-op CPU access hooks; unknown/cacheable exported
backing is blocked until a separately reviewed ownership/synchronization solution exists.
Do not repair that with an assumed `DMA_BUF_IOCTL_SYNC` effect.

## Process-context sequence for a future implementation

1. Default off. Before decoding, verify source/module/client identity and allocation origin,
   CREATE/REQBUFS flags, exporter type, plane length and mapping policy. Retain the actual
   dma-buf fd or vb2 allocation and client surface independently through copying. No new
   allocation, mapping or file write in IRQ/spinlock context.
2. Preallocate bounded scratch/output and create a read-only mapping where permitted by
   that exporter. Reject unknown/unmappable storage; no fallback read through a physical
   address. Map before the measurement window and retain it across paired off/on runs.
3. At selected writer completion, pause **all submissions/requeues in that client**, including
   worker threads. Wait for any already submitted reference readers to complete successfully
   under a finite deadline; record the last completed job and empty in-flight set. Reject
   foreign clients through the hardware guard. A paused producer alone is insufficient.
4. In ordinary process context, snapshot allocation/writer identity and copy only the two
   selected ranges below. Do not insert extra cache operations into the coherent path.
   Require unchanged identity and retained storage after copying. Store to the preallocated
   pool, resume submissions, then hash/serialize outside the paused interval. Stop/discard
   on timeout, error, overflow, changed writer, unsupported cache policy or lost retention.
5. A same-generation pre-reader checkpoint may compare against the completed-write snapshot
   only when that allocation remains retained and all preceding readers have completed.
   Never label a snapshot of a new writer as the old reference merely because index/POC
   matches. This second checkpoint needs its own bounded slot in the plan.

DQBUF plus `msync`, or merely seeing no `dma_sync_*` in AVD, is not this contract.
Any implementation that cannot enforce the pause/in-flight/retention sequence must return
an explicit blocked result. A kernel alternative also needs a reviewed lifetime pin and
process-context worker; it must not hash entire buffers while holding a spinlock or in IRQ.

## Ranges and limits

For initial 448×240 NV12 qualification only:

- Compression: `[161280,338432)`, 177152 bytes (four regions retained separately in metadata).
- MV: `[length-7168,length)`, where length is exactly 345600 or 368128 from the verified run.
- At most **184320 copied bytes/snapshot**, **8 snapshots/campaign**, **1474560 bytes total**
  preallocated copy pool; each retained mapping at most 368128 bytes. Allocation/table
  counts and descriptor metadata must also be fixed before a future run. No allocation gap
  or full-frame hash in this observer.
- Initial slots: three RPS_E writer snapshots and one RPS_B control per client. The control
  picture's identity comes from its same-run trace, not an assumed POC. Adding pre-reader
  checkpoints replaces slots or requires a separately reviewed budget; it cannot silently
  exceed eight.
- Copy interval maximum 20 ms; drain/pause maximum 2 s; each decoder run and the overall
  eight-workload off/on campaign retain finite external deadlines (proposed 120 s/run,
  20 min/campaign). A deadline is a rejection threshold, not a guarantee that scheduling
  or a memory access completes in time. Watchdog/guard remains outside the worker.

Each snapshot needs run UUID, context generation, allocation generation/index, writer
picture/decode index and POC, completion identity, source/build/corpus/encoded-input hashes,
cache/allocation policy, ranges and timestamps before/after copying. Preserve raw bytes
privately until their interpretation/publication is reviewed; publish normalized identity,
range hashes and statuses without addresses or unrelated memory. Never reconstruct missing
allocation or lifetime evidence from filenames or an earlier run.

## Observation disturbance and acceptance

The future default-off recorder must first pass source/build, strict malformed/range/identity,
retention and lifecycle tests. Its admission implementation must prove facts instead of
trusting this file's synthetic fixture booleans. No-device tests here reject wrong generation,
active readers, missing completion/retention/mapping, IRQ, cacheable/unknown policy, bad extent,
integer overflow, excessive byte/slot/time budgets, errors and disabled operation.

Hardware is a separate reviewed campaign using an exclusive guard and fresh run root.
Off and on both use the same pause/drain/mapping/preallocation/logging operations; only
selected copying differs. Preserve exact all-frame pixel hashes and reference/selected-command
projections. Accept observation only if off/on retain the same B exact/E known-wrong outputs,
no new error/timeout/foreign client, zero lost records and healthy final state. Copying,
quiescing or timing changes may still perturb behavior; unchanged output bounds the observed
effect for those runs and does not establish perfect noninterference.

## Interpret results conservatively

Different opaque bytes suggest hypotheses to test: incomplete overwrite, undefined padding,
allocation/lifetime, unobserved inputs, timing or firmware state. They do not identify the
responsible layer. Equal selected ranges constrain that sample and instant; they do not rule
out omitted ranges, firmware/cache state or a later read. A same-writer change between two
quiescent checkpoints is stronger evidence of an unaccounted write, but still requires proof
that both checkpoints and identities are valid.

Parent [driver #42](https://github.com/iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request/issues/42) retains the
actual correction, RPS_B/RPS_E outputs, complete codec pass sets and concurrency gates.
No support-count change or firmware-by-elimination conclusion follows from this design.
